verdicts.trueWording: She drops information on us after-the-fact but in ways that point forward
verdicts.note: Live page (blackgate.com, 200 OK, raw HTML stripped). Sentence appears verbatim under the 'First Person Slow Burn Thriller' heading; both limbs (after-the-fact, points forward) supported by the following gloss about mysterious strangers meaning danger 'Right Now'.

verdicts.trueWording: She exploits the fact we know what genre we are reading
verdicts.note: Live page, raw. Verbatim. Every limb supported: the sentence answers Page's own question 'So how does Robin Hobb keep the Thriller plot alive?' and is followed by 'We don't need a point-of-view shift to tell us that the ninjas have arrived.'

verdicts.trueWording: a country house Gothic from the point of view of the moody denizens
verdicts.note: Live page, raw. Verbatim substring; full page sentence adds 'of the moody denizens', so 'its denizens' is supported. Said of Fool's Assassin in the opening paragraphs.

verdicts.trueWording: They are people who are at the lower echelons of the economic strata
verdicts.note: Live page (lightspeedmagazine.com, 200 OK, raw). Verbatim. The question that prompts it names The Inheritance & Other Stories, 'featuring short fiction from throughout your career', so the short-fiction limb is supported by context; Hobb's own words are 'many of the characters in my stories'.

verdicts.trueWording: in the spectrum of fantasy people who actually work every day for a living and have a tight budget can seem like they're poor
verdicts.note: Live page, raw. Verbatim, and every limb (fantasy, work every day, tight budget, seem poor) is in the one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: we hunted and fished a lot for food... we had to put that food up for the winter
verdicts.note: Live page, raw. The quotation is verbatim, and the Alaskan-upbringing/food-preservation limbs are supported. But the passage is Hobb's answer to whether novelists should move to Alaska (about what a self-reliant location offers), not a statement about her fiction; she nowhere links putting food up to a survival economy in her work. The nearest real-life-to-work attribution on the page is geographic: 'There are a lot of things that come from real life into my written work, such as seismic activity, and lahars, and tidal waves.'
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: as the source of the survival economy in her work

verdicts.trueWording: They simply have something they want to get done, and it is more important to them than anything your protagonist wants to do
verdicts.note: Live host returned 403 to curl; recovered via Wayback raw capture 20250808211906id_ (200, 46KB). Verbatim. Byline confirmed in the page's JSON-LD: "author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Tayan Hatch"}; dated 2024-12-19. The 'outweighs the protagonist's aim' limb is the sentence's own second clause.

verdicts.trueWording: You have to put it on like a coat and say, 'Now I believe everything you believe.'
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (same as 216). Verbatim. Introduced by Hatch as 'the importance of fully embodying a villain's perspective', supporting the 'a character's viewpoint' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: You could take that whole trilogy and rewrite it from his point of view, and he would be a tragic hero
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (same as 216). Verbatim, and named to Regal of the Farseer Trilogy in the immediately preceding sentences.

verdicts.trueWording: I'm not talking about world building here. I will mention briefly: coinage or money value, major religions, calendar with seasonal names and year dates
verdicts.note: Live page (robinhobb.com, 200 OK, raw). The list is verbatim, so the three named items are fully supported. But Hobb introduces the list by expressly bracketing the topic off - 'I'm not talking about world building here' - and then turns to what she does keep: 'But what I'm discussing here is the writer keeping the story straight' (time line and glossary). The page does not say she keeps records of coinage, religions or the calendar.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that these are worldbuilding records she keeps

verdicts.trueWording: Not with a page number or even a chapter... but the incident. As in, 'Joe is met in the tavern shortly before the disastrous river crossing.'
verdicts.note: Live page, raw. Verbatim. Every limb supported in one passage: 'I needed my own glossary', 'I also found it handy to include when that character first appeared. Not with a page number or even a chapter, as those always change in the construction of a book, but the incident.'

verdicts.trueWording: Each chapter begins with an epigraph-a snippet of in-world text ranging from historical treatises and herbalist journals to fragments of folklore and political propaganda
verdicts.note: Live host returned 403 to curl; recovered via Wayback raw capture 20260607133057id_ (200, 60KB). Verbatim, in section '2.2 The Epigraphs: World-Building through Fragmented History'. Note the page's list also includes herbalist journals, which the claim omits without misstating.

verdicts.trueWording: the dry, academic tone of an epigraph about the 'glory' of the Farseer line is immediately followed by a scene depicting the brutal, unglamorous reality of Fitz's life
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (same as 221). Verbatim, under the 'Tonal Contrast' bullet in section 2.2.

verdicts.trueWording: By dedicating thousands of words to the mundane details of Fitz's daily existence... Hobb forces the reader to inhabit the protagonist's rhythm of life
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (same as 221). Verbatim, in section 2.3 'The "Slow Burn" as Psychological Immersion'; the causal 'attributes the slow burn to' limb is the sentence's own structure.
